subject: Commit vs Pipeline: Mini-cert sprint + actions (please review)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commit vs Pipeline: Mini-cert sprint + actions (please review)

Team — putting this thread together to run a tight, 3-day mini-sprint to remove ambiguity from our Commit / Best Case / Pipeline buckets before we run Q3 forecasts. Quick context: Acme is sensitive to how we classify their expansion opportunity (large cross-sell). Procurement asked for clear definitions and a single point of truth we can share in the renewal packet.

Goal: align sellers + AEs + ops on 3 quick deliverables by end of day Friday:
- A one-page “decision tree” (attached) that sellers can use live in calls.
- A 10-minute certification quiz for reps (pass threshold 80%) so we can show adoption.
- A short update to HubSpot deal stages (readonly doc linked below) so downstream reports are consistent.

Immediate asks:
1) Rishi — can you review the one-pager and flag any runtime/pricing implications (tokens, routing fallback) so we avoid misclassification that masks revenue?
2) Marissa — please coordinate the quiz and add sprint calendar invite (I attached an .ics).
3) Karthik — want your ops eyes on the HubSpot stage mapping and a 10-line change log we can hand to finance.

I added Sarah (Acme) here so they see the transparency as we align; we’ll only share the final one-pager and the HubSpot snapshot.

Attachments: redwood-commit-vs-pipeline-onepager.pdf, sprint-calendar-invite.ics

Thanks — short & focused. I’ll run a 15-min sync Friday AM to accept final signoffs.

— Jasmine Liu
Revenue Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit vs Pipeline: Mini-cert sprint + actions (please review)

Thanks, Jasmine — reviewed the one-pager quickly. High level notes:
- The definition for "Commit" looks solid but we need a standard timestamp requirement: seller must have signed LOE or verbally committed with legal hold + PO in flight. Without a timebound signal we risk backfilling.
- "Best Case" should explicitly exclude deals without an assigned exec sponsor; that’s been a repeat source of optimistic BestCase entries.
- Operational impact: if we require PO/LOE prior to Commit, routing to Dedicated SKU may need an override flag in the request metadata (I can add this to the technical spec).

I’ll add inline comments in the PDF and push a short PR to the ops doc. Referencing the attached line items I think will keep Finance happy.

Quick ask for Sarah: Sarah — would your procurement team accept a normalized "PO in flight" status (procurement email + expected PO date) as sufficient for Commit? If not, say so and we'll adjust.

-Rishi
Senior Deal Strategist
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 12:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit vs Pipeline: Mini-cert sprint + actions (please review)

Rishi — thanks for the clarity. Acme's procurement would accept a PO-in-flight artifact (email from procurement with an expected PO date) for Commit. We cannot make legal sign-offs public, so the minimum will be procurement confirmation + expected PO date. That should work for our internal tracking and for your finance snapshot.

I appreciate you including us — the one-pager reads well from our POV.

- Sarah
Procurement Lead, Acme Corporation
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit vs Pipeline: Mini-cert sprint + actions (please review)

All — I created the 10-question mini-cert and uploaded answers (sprint plan attached). Plan: send to 12 reps on Monday, auto-grade, and we’ll report pass rates to finance and the account team.

Highlights of quiz items: scenario-based classification (4 items), hubspot stage mapping (3 items), and one question on "what counts as PO in flight" (with Sarah's sample acceptable answer). I attached the answers key for ops to validate.

Also added the sprint calendar invite and a 15-minute signoff meeting Friday 8:30 AM (sprint close).

Attachments: mini-cert-quiz-answers-key.csv, sprint-calendar-invite.ics

-M
RevOps Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit vs Pipeline: Mini-cert sprint + actions (please review)

Quick readout from ops: I've updated the HubSpot stage mapping doc with a 6-line change log (see Drive link). Key operational changes we implemented:
- New boolean field: "po_in_flight" (true/false) on the opportunity object.
- Commit stage requires either po_in_flight=true OR signed LOE uploaded to the deal attachments.
- Best Case requires assigned exec sponsor + ARR estimate with confidence score >=70.

I validated the change in sandbox and will push to production next Tuesday during the maintenance window.

Next steps: Jasmine to finalize the one-pager with Rishi's inline notes and share a final PDF with Acme; Marissa to distribute the quiz Monday and compile pass rates by Wednesday.

Thanks everyone — happy to discuss if we need to relax any gating rules for specific strategic deals.

-Karthik
Director, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference
